HGEN-CTX-G1.title: Community garden plot holder handbook
HGEN-CTX-G1.text:
Maple Street Community Garden - Plot Holder Handbook

Welcome to Maple Street Community Garden. This handbook covers what every plot holder agrees to when they accept a plot. Please keep it somewhere you can find it; most questions we get during the season are answered here.

Fees
The annual plot fee is $45 for a standard 10 x 12 foot bed. Households that qualify for the city's utility assistance program pay a reduced fee of $20. Fees are due before you receive the shed code. Fees are not refunded after June 1, but if you give up your plot before then we refund half.

Getting started
New plot holders must attend one orientation. This season there are two: Saturday, May 16 at 10 am and Wednesday, May 20 at 6:30 pm, both at the tool shed by the north gate. Orientation takes about 45 minutes and covers the water system, compost bins, and the shed.

Your plot must be cleared of weeds and planted within 21 days of the date you are assigned it. If a plot is still bare after 21 days, the garden coordinator will send one reminder email. If nothing has changed seven days after the reminder, the plot is offered to the next household on the waiting list. We do this because the waiting list is currently 38 households long.

Workdays
Every plot holder contributes six hours of shared work per season. The easiest way is to come to our monthly workdays, held on the first Saturday of each month from 9 am to noon. Hours can also be earned by turning the compost, mowing the paths, or helping at the fall harvest swap. Log your hours on the clipboard inside the shed door. Plot holders who have logged fewer than three hours by August 1 will get a friendly check-in; we would rather help you find hours than lose you.

Watering
Water only before 9 am or after 6 pm. Midday watering wastes water and scorches leaves, and the city meter reads us as a single household. Hoses must be coiled back on their reels after use. Please do not leave sprinklers running unattended.

Being away
If you will be away for more than a week during the growing season, arrange a plot buddy to water and harvest for you, and let the coordinator know who it is. Absences longer than three weeks require written notice to the coordinator in advance, so we do not mistake your plot for an abandoned one. You can find a plot buddy through the garden group chat or ask the coordinator to match you with someone.

Growing rules
No synthetic pesticides or herbicides anywhere in the garden. Plants may not grow taller than six feet or shade a neighboring plot. Invasive plants such as mint must be grown in a container sunk into the bed. Diseased plant material goes in the black bin by the gate, never in the compost.

The shed
The shed code changes on the first of every month and is sent by text to all paid plot holders. Tools are shared; please clean them and hang them back where you found them. Personal tools can be stored in the labeled cubbies but the garden is not responsible for them.

Contact
Garden coordinator: Dana Whitfield, coordinator@maplestreetgarden.org. Dana checks email on weekday evenings. For anything urgent at the garden, such as a burst pipe, call the city parks line posted on the shed door.

HGEN-CTX-C1.title: Family lake trip planning notes
HGEN-CTX-C1.text:
Lake trip planning - shared notes (Okafor family)

Dates: we fly out Friday 16 October and come back Sunday 25 October. Cabin is Pine Hollow, unit 4, at Lake Averill.

Flights
Outbound is flight NW 318 which departs 9:40 am from Terminal 2. We should be at the airport two hours before. Return is Sunday 25 October at 4:05 pm.

Cabin
Total for the cabin is $2,400 for the whole stay. We paid the $600 deposit on 3 August, so the balance of $1,800 is due by October 1. Check-in is Friday 16 October from 3 pm, so we can drive straight there from the airport. Checkout is 10 am on the last day. The cabin sleeps six.

Who is coming
Mom, Dad, Chidi, Ada, Uncle Femi and Grace. Six people, so we need one mid-size car.

Car
Mid-size SUV booked with the rental desk at the airport, pick-up Friday afternoon. Grace is the second driver.

Logistics and packing (added later by Chidi)
Because of our 7:15 am flight on the Friday, we need to leave the house by 4:45 am. Dad will do the drive and leave the car in long-term parking. The cabin owner emailed to say the remaining $1,600 is due by October 9, not the first, and that it can be paid by bank transfer. Also note check-in is Saturday, so we might need a hotel near the airport on Friday night, or we just drive slowly and have a long lunch. Ada says her friend Lina may come too, which would make seven of us.

Packing: warm layers, rain jackets, board games, the good coffee, swimsuits for the hot tub.

To do
- Pay cabin balance (Mom)
- Confirm car seat not needed (Ada)
- Book hotel for Friday night? (depends on check-in)
- Print boarding passes the night before

HGEN-CTX-G2.title: Office move staff FAQ
HGEN-CTX-G2.text:
Brightwater Studio - Move to the Harlow Building: Staff FAQ

We are moving from our current office on Fenwick Road to floors 3 and 4 of the Harlow Building, 220 Quay Street. This FAQ collects the answers to what people have asked so far. It will be updated as details are confirmed; the version date is at the bottom.

When is the move?
The last working day at Fenwick Road is Friday 13 November. The movers come over that weekend. The Harlow Building opens for us on Monday 16 November. Please work from home on Friday 13 November if you can; the office will be open but noisy and partly packed.

What do I need to pack, and by when?
Everyone gets two labelled crates. Put anything you want moved to your new desk into your crates and leave them at your desk by Thursday 12 November at 4 pm. Crates are collected after 4 pm that day. Anything left loose on or under a desk after that will be treated as unwanted and cleared. Plants are welcome but must travel in a crate or go home with you.

What about my monitor, dock and chair?
Company monitors, docks and keyboards stay where they are. Do not unplug them; IT will label and move all company equipment and set it up at the new desks before Monday. Personal equipment, including personal second monitors, footrests and chairs you bought yourself, must be taken home by Friday 13 November. The movers are not insured to carry personal items.

Do I have an assigned desk at Harlow?
For the first two weeks, desks are assigned by team and there is a seating plan on the wiki, so no booking needed. From Monday 30 November we switch to booked desks using the Deskly app. Each team keeps a home zone, but individual desks are booked daily.

Is there parking?
There is no free staff parking at the Harlow Building. The studio will subsidise monthly permits at the Canal Street garage, which works out to $60/month for staff after the subsidy. Permits are limited to 25 spaces and are allocated first come, first served. Apply through the People team form by Friday 6 November. There is a covered, secure bike cage on the ground floor with 40 spaces and showers on floor 3.

What happens to the kitchen and fridge?
The Fenwick Road fridge will be emptied and cleaned on Wednesday 11 November. Anything left inside at 5 pm that day will be thrown away. The new kitchen on floor 4 has two fridges, a dishwasher and a coffee machine.

What about post and deliveries?
From Monday 16 November, use 220 Quay Street as the delivery address. Post sent to Fenwick Road will be forwarded for three months. Personal online orders should not be delivered to the office during move week.

Who do I ask?
Questions about desks and equipment go to IT at the helpdesk channel. Questions about parking, access cards and the seating plan go to Tomasz Lindgren in the People team. Access cards for Harlow will be handed out at the front desk on Monday 16 November from 8:30 am; bring your current card to exchange.

Version date: 2 November.

items.question: Affect or effect?
items.answer: **Affect** is usually the verb, meaning to influence something. **Effect** is usually the noun, meaning the result. So a change can affect you, and it has an effect on you. The exception is "effect change," meaning to bring it about.

items.question: Why does my phone battery die so much faster when it's cold outside?
items.answer: Cold slows down the chemical reactions inside a lithium-ion battery, so it can't release its stored energy as quickly. That makes the voltage sag, and your phone reads that as a low battery and shuts down sooner. It's usually temporary, the capacity comes back once the phone warms up.

items.question: I just got assigned a plot at the community garden. What do I actually have to do in the first month so I don't lose it?
items.answer: The main deadline is the 21-day rule: your plot has to be cleared of weeds and planted within 21 days of the day it was assigned, or you get one reminder email and then it goes to the next household on the waiting list. You also need to attend one orientation, and fees are due before you get the shed code.

items.question: Why not the other day though?
conversation: OTHER PERSON: Okay so I got the van from my cousin, but only for one day this weekend.
OTHER PERSON: Either Saturday, but I have to have it back by 2, or Sunday, the whole day, but then Mike can't help because he's got his kid's tournament.
USER (spoken): And the new place, when can you get the keys?
OTHER PERSON: Keys are Saturday at 9 at the earliest. And the old place is a third floor walk-up, no elevator.
OTHER PERSON: There's not that much stuff though, maybe a couch, a bed, a dresser and like twenty boxes.
OTHER PERSON (heard): So what do you think, Saturday or Sunday?

NATIVELY: Saturday, I think. The keys are ready at 9, so we can load up in the morning and still have the van back by 2. Sunday gives us more hours, but losing Mike on a third floor walk-up with a couch and a bed is a bigger problem than a short day. If we start at 9 sharp and keep it tight, Saturday works.
items.answer: Sunday's the problem, not the day itself. We'd have the van all day, which is nice, but Mike's out because of his kid's tournament, and that's the wrong day to lose him. It's a third floor walk-up with no elevator, and the couch and bed are the heavy part. Saturday we get the keys at 9 and still have the van back by 2, so we just have to move fast.

items.question: So what time do we actually have to leave the house on the Friday? I need to set an alarm.
items.answer:
The notes say leave the house by **4:45 am** on the Friday. That's built around the 7:15 am flight, so set your alarm for around 4, and Dad's doing the drive and leaving the car in long-term parking.

One thing though, the notes contradict themselves on the flight time. The flight section says outbound NW 318 departs 9:40 am, while the later logistics note says 7:15 am. Worth confirming which is right before you set that alarm.

items.question: Which one would you actually go with?
conversation: USER (typed to Natively): Give me five ideas for a leaving gift for a coworker who's really into climbing. Budget is about 40 bucks from the team.

NATIVELY: For a climber, gear they'll actually use beats a keepsake. Five solid options around forty dollars from the team:

1. A chalk bag, since it's personal and gets used every session.
2. A guidebook to a crag or area they've been wanting to visit.
3. A set of climbing-specific hand balm and tape for sore skin.
4. A carabiner keyring or small accessory they can clip to a harness.
5. A gift card to a local climbing gym or gear shop, so they pick their own.
